source.title: Zero-Shot Generalization during Instruction Tuning: Insights from Similarity and Granularity
source.authors: Bing-Xiang He; Ning Ding; Cheng Qian; Jia Deng; Ganqu Cui; Lifan Yuan; Huan-ang Gao; Hui-Min Chen; Zhi-Yuan Liu; Mao-Song Sun

record.file_problem: The provided title does not match the paper text: the text is titled “The Right Time Matters: Data Arrangement Affects Zero-Shot Generalization in Instruction Tuning.” The text otherwise presents a full paper and identifies arXiv:2406.11721.
record.tranche_reason: It measures unseen-task loss over instruction-tuning checkpoints, which bears on the training-time trajectory claim, but it does not use the original double-descent setup.
record.gate_note: The relevant results track loss on unseen test data across instruction-tuning steps. The paper reports qualitative trajectory descriptions and some step locations, but no loss values for the curves in the supplied text. Results about similarity metrics are included only where they report test-loss trajectories. No result tests model size, the interpolation threshold, or increasing sample size near that threshold.
record.test_reason: The study tracks unseen-task cross-entropy loss over a single epoch of instruction tuning of LLaMA-2-7B, varying the order of training data. It never mentions or cites double descent. It does not sweep model size, sample count or capacity. It does not train toward interpolation or over multiple epochs, and it does not vary label noise. Its loss-over-steps curves measure how fast generalization arrives in a one-pass fine-tune, not an epoch-wise fall-rise-fall test curve. So its results cannot bear on whether V2 or any other version holds. Closest fit is T6; the relation enum has no 'neither' option, so 'discusses' is used loosely.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also conclude that zero-shot generalization in instruction tuning is a form of instance-level, similarity-based generalization between training and test data. They also conclude that loss is a more stable indicator than ROUGE, Exact-Match or RM score.
record.recipe_differences: The study tracks unseen-task loss during instruction tuning and varies data order; it does not sweep model size or training-set size around an interpolation threshold.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss trajectories vary with data arrangement (random, round-robin, cluster, nearest-first, farthest-first, and TMA strategies), data granularity, test-data subset/seed, and dataset. The appendix reports differing task-level curve patterns across test-data seeds.

fits_no_version.finding: In single-epoch instruction tuning of LLaMA-2-7B, unseen-task loss drops sharply when training examples similar to the test set are encountered. Placing such examples earlier gives faster and lower loss, and instance-level ordering beats task-cluster ordering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Zero-shot generalization in instruction tuning is driven by instance-level similarity between training and test data, and the timing of exposure to similar data shapes the loss trajectory.

fits_no_version.finding: Unseen-task loss reaches its minimum within about 50 steps (around 160 examples for ROUGE gains) across NIV2, P3 and Flan-mini.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Zero-shot generalization from instruction tuning emerges very early in training.

record.problems: The authors state that experiments were limited to LLaMA-2-7B with a few runs due to computational and storage constraints. The supplied text gives qualitative curve descriptions rather than numerical loss values for the relevant trajectories. The authors also note that their similarity measures lack a strong theoretical foundation.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results were omitted for the row limit. The appendix's figures varying test-data seeds are described qualitatively but are not separately rowed because they do not report a separately quantified double-descent trajectory.

untested.parts: There is no multi-epoch training toward interpolation; one epoch of instruction tuning is not the epoch-wise setting.
No sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No label noise or regularization manipulation.

record.verdict_notes: The record's file_problem notes a title mismatch, so this paper may have been retrieved in error for the double-descent search. The paper contains no reference to double descent or interpolation. Training is 1 epoch at learning rate 1e-6, so the epoch-wise regime of V2 is never reached. The reader's 'challenges' label on V2 has been removed.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or interpolation-threshold measurement.
Tests loss over instruction-tuning steps in LLaMA-2-7B, not the claim across deep networks generally or a controlled sweep over training epochs in the original settings.
No comparison of increasing training-set size near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes or test of general double descent.
Similarity is compared with loss, but no single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak location across axes.
No test of label noise, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameter number.

relation.reason: Applicable as discussion of related generalization dynamics only: the text does not explicitly mention, cite, assume, use, or test double descent.

tranche.reason: The experiments investigate early zero-shot generalization and data arrangement, without testing or using a double-descent claim. Early minima and the two reported task-level trends do not establish a fall-rise-fall trajectory.

source_check.notes: The less-than-50-step result concerns aggregate loss on NIV2, P3 and Flan-mini, not every individual task or later data-arrangement experiment. The supplied text is the April 2025 v2 with a revised title; single-epoch training alone does not exclude V2.
